name: An Everfull Flask

rarity.note: True wrought survival; modest power, absolute scarcity.

summary: Small Concord flasks, palm-sized, that always hold one more drink of whatever they last held — water stays water, wine stays wine, and one flask in a Wealdmark cellar has held the same cup of cider for eight hundred years. They were lunch-boxes once. Now each is named, insured, and fought over, because a flask that always holds clean water is worth a caravan's ransom anywhere past the last well.
origin: Concord of Weavers — common household ware, pre-Sundering; the working was mass-produced then
current_whereabouts: Seven known: two Well-Sister wells, one Storm-Bound strongbox, one Reeve's court evidence-vault, three private.
properties: Always holds exactly one more drink of its last contents
Emptied fully — poured to the last drop — it forgets and must be refilled once to begin again
Sour liquid sours permanently; the flasks teach their keepers sobriety
keepers: As above; the Censer lists them as 'contained' but has never seized one — every keeper has lawful papers, mostly Septuary-certified inheritance.
value_or_danger: A caravan's ransom. In a drought year: whatever the buyer has, plus what he'll owe.
adventure_hooks: An eighth flask surfaces claiming to hold 'the same cider as the Wealdmark one' — impossible, unless both were filled from the same barrel before the Sundering.
Players escort an empty flask across the deep dunes to be filled at Akhmat's Tears: the League wants to know if the goddess's water remembers.
